c.tagline: Morocco's desert film capital and gateway to the Sahara.

taxi.fareNote: Petits taxis are shared beige cabs for short hops around town; there are no ride-hailing apps, so agree the meter or a flat fare before setting off. Grands taxis (older Mercedes) handle longer runs to Ait Benhaddou and the valleys.

emergency.note: 19 reaches the police (Surete Nationale) in towns and 15 is the ambulance/medical service; 177 reaches the Gendarmerie Royale on rural roads outside the city.

avoid.reason: Faux guides and studio-tour touts cluster around Taourirt Kasbah and the film studios; agree taxi and tour prices before setting off.

hood_desc: The walkable downtown along Avenue Mohammed V, packed with cafes, restaurants, shops and tour agencies; the easiest base for first-timers who want everything within reach.
The historic quarter around the earthen Kasbah of Taourirt and the Cinema Museum, opposite the artisan center; best for travelers who want sights and old-Morocco atmosphere on their doorstep.
A quieter district just south of the center with intimate riads and guesthouses, Atlas Mountain views and easy reach of the Atlas Film Studios; suits those wanting calm over bustle.
A residential neighborhood by the hospital and airport on the northwest edge of town; practical and low-key, a handy quiet spot before flying or driving on.
The famous fortified ksar village 30 km west, a UNESCO World Heritage kasbah and film backdrop; an overnight stay lets you photograph it at sunrise before the day crowds arrive.

water.note: Locals drink the chlorinated tap water, but most travelers stick to bottled to avoid stomach upsets.

transit.hours: There is no scheduled service; petits taxis run through the day and grands taxis and coaches leave from the gare routiere, thinning out after dark.
transit.note: Ouarzazate has no city bus, tram or metro network; getting around town relies on shared beige petits taxis, and longer hops use grands taxis and intercity coaches.
transit.pay: Petits taxis are paid in cash (dirhams) to the driver; short in-town rides cost only a few dirhams. There is no transit card.

bus: Supratours coaches to Marrakech, Agadir and the Draa Valley
Grands taxis to Ait Benhaddou, Zagora and Boumalne Dades
train: No rail service; the nearest station is Marrakech, about 4 hours by road over the Tizi n'Tichka pass

transit.m: Petit taxi to the town center (5-10 min)
Many hotels offer free or cheap airport pickup on request

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants; rounding up taxis and cafe bills is appreciated.
